description: Algorithmic reverb built from a chain of delays, filters and feedback loops. The display plots its impulse response: time left to right, frequency front to back, amplitude as the height of each line

params.text: Length of the reverb tail in seconds: roughly the time the reverberated signal takes to decay by -60dB
Character of the reverb, set by the mix of its internal delay taps
Cutoff of the high-pass filter inside the reverb, which keeps the reflections from turning muddy
Cutoff of the low-pass filter inside the reverb, which shortens the decay of the top end
How long the dry signal is delayed before the reverb processes it. In a room this is the time sound takes to reach the nearest wall and return, about 18ms for a wall 3m away
Stereo spread of the reverberated signal; at 0% it is mono, and it is then mixed with a dry signal that may be stereo
Balance between the dry input and the reverberated signal
How far the voltage at the TIME input moves the reverb time, and in which direction
How far the voltage at the MORPH input moves the character, and in which direction
How far the voltage at the HP input moves the high-pass cutoff, and in which direction
How far the voltage at the LP input moves the low-pass cutoff, and in which direction
How far the voltage at the WIDTH input moves the stereo spread, and in which direction
How far the voltage at the MIX input moves the dry and wet balance, and in which direction
Hold to freeze the reverb: its internal state is held and incoming audio is blocked, so the tail runs on without end

inputs.text: CV over the character of the reverb
CV over the dry and wet balance
Audio in; with no cable in RIGHT this signal feeds both channels
Right channel of the audio in
A gate here freezes the reverb for as long as it is high, holding the tail and blocking incoming audio

outputs.text: Left channel out, the dry and processed signals mixed
Right channel out, the dry and processed signals mixed
